title: gitapex effectiveness-corpus.json (issue #1143)
description: Schema for effectiveness-corpus.json: the held-out corpus naming which skills participate in a future effectiveness study (issue #1137 sub-task 3, contingent on this issue's own result), which real files supply each skill's independently-measured quality outcome, and which held-out split (selection/test, see effectiveness-corpus-methodology.md) each belongs to. This file pins shape only, the same split this repository's other schemas already draw between shape (here) and procedure (effectiveness-corpus-methodology.md, the same way eval-run.schema.json defers to scorer-gated-skill-edits/SKILL.md's own Procedure step 7 for what a run record must capture).

methodology_doc.description: Repository-relative path to the methodology document this corpus is governed by.

entries.description: One entry per skill in the corpus, sorted by skill name for a stable diff across edits (the same convention eval-scores.schema.json's own scores[] states for fixture_id).

skill.description: The skill's directory name under skills/, matching its evals/<skill>/ directory name 1:1 (verified repository convention: gitapex_detect_touched_eval_skills.py's own docstring, confirmed empirically against this repository's current skills/ and evals/ listings).

skill_md.description: Repository-relative path to this skill's SKILL.md.

eval_yaml.description: Repository-relative path to this skill's own evals/<skill>/eval.yaml, the suite gitapex_run_eval_suite.py runs to obtain this entry's real quality-outcome label.

split.description: Which held-out split this skill belongs to (see effectiveness-corpus-methodology.md's own 'Held-out split' section for the deterministic assignment rule). Only these two values -- no train split, since this corpus does not gate an edit the way scorer-gated-skill-edits' own three-way split does.

knownPriorResult.description: Optional. A real, already-committed eval-scores.schema.json-conformant result file for this skill's own suite, cited for provenance and cross-reference only -- gitapex_run_effectiveness_correlation.py always computes its own fresh y value (see methodology doc's 'End-to-end wiring' section) rather than reading this field as input, so a stale citation here can never silently skew a live correlation run.

source_file.description: Repository-relative path to the cited eval-scores.schema.json-conformant file.

mean_score.description: That file's own mean_score, copied verbatim for a reader who will not open it.

n_fixtures.description: That file's own n_fixtures, copied verbatim.

date.description: The run's own real calendar date, as recorded in its results/<date>-issue-<N>-<label>/ directory name.

caveat.description: Any disclosed scope limit on treating this citation as representative (e.g. a partial-subset gate-check run, not the skill's full committed corpus). Required, non-empty -- a citation with nothing to disclose still states that explicitly rather than omitting the field.
